body:
A NOTE TO CONSIDER, at Myk's request (chat, 2026-08-09). celld (https://celld.dev/) is a self-hosted, open-source implementation of Cloudflare's Durable Objects model: V8 + SQLite + LTX segment replication to an S3-compatible bucket, CAS-based ownership, ~20s failover, RPO=0, ~4MB per hibernated cell, ~4ms activation, ~1,000 cells per 8GB node. Myk's framing: a celld store as an ALTERNATIVE to a local one — possibly the solution for a hosted backend.

WHY IT FITS: a Loam store IS a durable object at the store granularity — single-writer reactor, one SQLite ground, isolation-first multi-tenancy. Store-per-cell buys placement, hibernation density, and failover for thousands of small personal stores without building an orchestrator. §15 (the browser peer) already settled the seam: where the deltas sleep is a driver's business, and StoreBackend has four drivers today (memory, sqlite, archive, localStorage). A CellBackend is the fifth. The genuinely new work is the DOOR layer: serve speaks node:http; a cell speaks fetch handlers.

THE TWO BLOCKERS, both already named in this backlog:
1. ERASURE OVER LTX REPLICAS. The bucket retains historical segments, so a purged delta's bytes survive in old segments until retention or compaction. The erasure promise (full, provable — Myk, 2026-07-25, closed) would be FALSE over an LTX chain. Either the erasure fan-out learns replica retention, or T101 (crypto-shredding at rest) lands first — T101 is this ticket's natural prerequisite. Until then the only honest hosted posture is a T105-style receipt disclosure naming the replica tier as unprovable.
2. THE TRUST ROOT MOVES. Today the filesystem is the trust root (operator model, settled). In a cell runtime the effective root is the bucket + the celld nodes: bucket credentials hold every hosted store's seeds. A real relocation of the security boundary — a spec decision, never a default.

HARD CONSTRAINT: cells never finer than a store. Negation closure, constitutional reads and Schema resolution want the whole ground in one reactor; per-container or per-entity cells reopen H1-class holes.

DELIVERABLE WHEN OPENED: a working spec (.adlc/specs/) covering the CellBackend driver, the fetch-handler doors, the erasure posture (T101 prerequisite or disclosure interim), and the trust-boundary statement. Design-stage: the spec and every open question go to Myk before any code.

EDGES: T101 (crypto-shredding) is the erasure prerequisite. Relates T103 (a served store cannot pull — a cell-hosted store has the same pulse question).
title: A celld cell as the store's home — the hosted-backend candidate (DESIGN-STAGE, BACKGROUND)
